# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — JCAP (Jefferson Capital, Inc.)

**Prepared by:** Senior Underwriting Board | **Desk run:** 1 of 5 (complete: Bear/Base/Bull) | **T0:** $19.67 [Actual, live quote 2026-10-05]

---

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | JCAP — Jefferson Capital, Inc. (charged-off, insolvency & active consumer receivables; US/UK/Canada/LatAm) |
| Price T0 | $19.67 [Actual] |
| Market cap | $1.127B [Aggregator] |
| **Verdict** | **UNDEVALUED — Accumulate (value basis)** |
| Base IV | **$62.42** (prob 45%) |
| Bull IV | **$81.90** (prob 30%) |
| Bear IV | **$29.87** (prob 25%) |
| Probability-weighted EV | $60.13 [Arithmetic on desk values] |
| Margin of safety | 68.5% to Base; 67.3% on prob-weighted EV; even Bear is +52% above T0 |
| Neutral reverse DCF (desk) | −10.14% 10-yr CAGR implied by price |

The market is pricing a business whose cash flows **shrink ~10%/yr for a decade**. The company's own filings show the opposite: a $3.4B estimated-remaining-collections (ERC) pipeline growing +18% YoY, record deployments ($152.2M in Q2 2026; $185M in July 2026 — a monthly record), and a sector-leading 72.2% Cash Efficiency Ratio [Actual, PRIMARY P1, filed 2026-08-13]. The price is paying ~6x FY2025 GAAP earnings for what the filings describe as an asset-backed compounding flywheel.

---

## SECTION 1 — MACRO (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates:** 10y nominal 5.28%, real 2.92%; curve +0.45% and steepening; IG spread 1.49%, HY OAS 3.10% [Actual, as of 2026-10-01/02]. COE ANCHOR **9.01%** (rf_eff 5.28% + 0.895× loading × 4.17% premium) — used unchanged in Base/Bull; Bear adds +150bp stress to 10.50%.
- **Regime vector:** goldilocks 0.341, reflation 0.271, tightening 0.176, stagflation 0.130, recession 0.081 — headline goldilocks but contested (margin 0.070). News flow (2026-09-25) notes markets pricing **possible additional rate hikes** against CPI 3.35% / PCE 3.42%.
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` (severity 1, onset 2026-09-28; Hormuz disruption, Saudi pipeline attack). Transmission to JCAP is second-order: energy-driven inflation → sticky consumer delinquencies (**bull** for paper supply) but weaker repayment capacity and higher funding costs (**bear**).
- **Exposure map:** (i) Funding — $1.754B total debt, RCF upsized to $1.15B with only $226M drawn at 6/30/26 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; new marginal paper prices at **8.250%** (PRIMARY P4/P5) — the rising cost of growth is real and is embedded in my terminal ronic haircut. (ii) Consumer balance sheet — US consumer delinquencies at 4.8% of household debt, highest since 2017 [Estimate, Bloomberg 2026-02-10]; auto serious delinquency 5.2% in Q4 2025 [Estimate, NY Fed via americandefault.org]. Elevated stress is the *source* of JCAP's cheap supply — it cuts both ways and is why my Bear is a consumer-repayment shock, not an arbitrary cut.

---

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT

**Economic engines (mandate 1):**

a) **Transactional deliveries — portfolio purchases.** Deployments $152.2M in Q2 2026 (+21.5% YoY); July 2026 $185M monthly record across performing and non-performing auto [Actual, PRIMARY P1; Estimate, transcript 2026-08-20]. Portfolio revenue $165.3M in Q2. This is the growth engine: each deployment seeds multi-year collection cash flow.

b) **Captive installed base — the ERC annuity.** Owned receivables of $1.947B net carry an **ERC of $3,364.2M (+17.9% YoY)** [Actual, PRIMARY P1] — ~2.8x annualized collections at the current run-rate. This is a pipeline of *expected* (not contractually guaranteed) cash from assets the company owns; debtors cannot be compelled to pay, so it is an asset-backed floor, not a contracted backlog. Supporting it: **$480.7M committed forward flows** (contractual purchase agreements at pre-negotiated prices, per the company's own glossary in the Q2 call) [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Servicing revenue ($10.7M Q2; UK $8.9M) and the Bluestem credit-card book (net receivables $15.0M; $41.0M Q2 collections) are smaller recurring layers [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P2].

c) **Strategic optionality.** LatAm collections +52.5% YoY, UK +14.0%; legal-channel collections $64M in Q2 (+54% YoY) after process improvements that accelerated lawsuit filings; Mexico entry (brief claim — [Unconfirmed]); performing-auto expansion.

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** FY2025 net income $188.0M with SBC of only $17.0M already expensed in GAAP (deducted once, `sbc_treatment: deducted_in_cf`) [Actual, DATA 5]. FY2025: revenue $613.3M, net operating income $316.5M (51.6% margin), pre-tax $218.4M, OCF $269.0M, interest expense $105.8M [Actual, DATA 5/P3]. H1 2026: revenue $354.0M (+15%), net income $78.9M (−29.4% YoY) — the GAAP decline is opex-driven (court costs + IPO SBC), discussed in Section 9. TTM OCF exceeds NI+D&A by $61M on working-capital timing (recoveries, payables) [Actual, DATA 3] — excluded from my owner-earnings base, which sits at FY2025's $192.1M (the desk's reference base).

**Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3 each → /21 → 1.0–5.0):** switching/contractual lock-in **2** (forward-flow commitments); scale & cost **3** (sector-leading CER 72.2%; one of the very few players covering performing + charged-off + insolvency auto, secured and unsecured — PRIMARY P1); proprietary data/underwriting **2** ("analytically driven" pricing; legal-channel process edge); network effects **0**; regulatory barrier **1** (regulation is a risk, not a barrier); brand/franchise **1**; capital access **2** ($1.15B RCF, 8.25% notes — also the vulnerability). **Total 11/21 → 3.1/5.0, direction: improving** (scale and legal-channel compounding; capital structure intact post-buyback).

**Financial strength:** Net debt $1.731B vs equity $476M [Actual, DATA 6/P1]; leverage 1.71x adjusted EBITDA, improved from 1.76x [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; repaid the 2026 notes ($300M deposited 8/13) and added $100M of 8.250% 2030s (PRIMARY P4/P5); Fitch BB-/Positive [Unconfirmed — page CSS-gated; from indexed text only]; 3M shares repurchased for $59M in Jan 2026 to reduce sponsor overhang [Estimate, transcript]; $0.24/qtr dividend ≈ 4.9% yield at T0 [Actual, PRIMARY P1].

---

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION (desk inputs & departures)

| Input | Value | Default | Departure reason (dated evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame / rate | Equity, COE **9.01%** | same | None — anchor used; Bear +150bp stress per mandate 4 |
| base_cf | **$0.192B** (FY2025 owner earnings) | $0.159B TTM | TTM base is depressed by the H1 2026 opex ramp and WC swings (recoveries −$16.1M, AP/accruals −$22.4M; PRIMARY P1 CF statement). Desk values at FYE, so FY2025's $192.1M is the representative base; it equals reference_base_b within 2%, so no WC deduction applies |
| Base growth y1–5 | **−14% / +6% / +10% / +9% / +7%** | held at $0.085B/$0.087B then +4.2% | The DEFAULTS levels are an artifact of a broken prior-year EPS base: the release's Q2 2025 comparative diluted share count (2,843k) is a filing error vs ~55–58M actual shares outstanding (PRIMARY P1), producing the phantom "−55.6% current-FY EPS" and $0.085B year-1 level. The consensus *levels* themselves corroborate my path: current-FY EPS $3.00 × 57.4M sh ≈ $172M, vs H1 2026 net income $78.9M (annualized ~$150–165M at FY2025's H2/H1 ratio of 0.68) and FY2025 $188M [Actual, DATA 4/P1]. Year 1 −14% = the real opex compression; years 3–5 (+8.7% avg) are below the +18% ERC growth and below the p90 (48.7%) for this cohort |
| Fade / terminal | **5-yr fade; g 3.75%; ronic 25.0%** | g 3.75%; ronic 30.4% | ronic haircut: the default's 66.2% r_tc is measured on a 3-year record (2023–2025) in an elevated-delinquency environment; marginal funding now costs 8.250% (PRIMARY P4, filed 2026-08-21) with markets pricing possible hikes (DATA 1.6, 2026-09-25). 25% = FY2025 return on stockholders' equity ($316.5M NOI / $476M equity ≈ 66% pre-interest; after ~$106M interest and tax, ROE ~39%) discounted for the higher-cost marginal capital and the legal-channel cost mix shift |
| Shares | 57,425,536 (default) | same | None — matches 57,435,586 issued at 6/30/26 [Actual, P1]; DATA 6B's 30.015M filed average is flagged unverified and inconsistent with the release |
| Life | Perpetual | — | Portfolio continuously replaced: H1 2026 purchases $313.8M vs collections applied $308.4M + $480.7M forward flows (PRIMARY P1); no licence/concession expiry |

**Desk terminal:** g 3.75% / ronic 25.0% → payout 1 − g/ronic = 85%; implied exit multiple ≈ (0.85)/(9.01%−3.75%) ≈ **16.2x year-6 cash flow**, vs the financials sector trailing-P/E band median 11.7x / p75 17.9x [Aggregator, DATA 8.5] — i.e., at or below the band's top quartile for a business growing above the economy with 72.2% cash efficiency. Stated plainly: my Base ($62.42) sits **well above** the consensus PT band ($24–30, mean $28.20) and 2.3x the desk's reference value ($27.56). The gap is not in levels — analysts' own EPS path ($3.00 → $3.08) matches my cash-flow levels — it is entirely in terminal multiple/growth: sell-side prices JCAP as a ~6–8x-multiple credit shop; the filings support an asset-backed compounding flywheel. That disagreement *is* the crux below.

**Neutral reverse DCF (mandate 3b):** under the neutral structure the price implies **−10.14% 10-yr CAGR** — cash flows shrinking a decade.
